However, his profile is fundamentally full-stack and backend-heavy — Java, Spring Boot, Kafka, and microservices dominate every role, with React and TypeScript appearing as secondary tools alongside deep backend infrastructure work. There is no evidence of dedicated product-facing frontend ownership, consumer-grade UI work, or genuine growth engineering (signup flows, activation, conversion experimentation). The profile reads as enterprise B2B internal tooling throughout with no product surface, capping at score 2. Additionally, the resume shows strong AI-generation signals with near-verbatim JD language and implausibly polished bullet framing inconsistent with the backend-heavy work history.

There is insufficient evidence of dedicated, professional frontend product ownership to support a score above 2, and the heavy AI-generation signals across the resume raise credibility concerns about the specificity of the claimed growth engineering metrics.

Qualifying dedicated frontend experience does not meet the 4-year hard minimum, and the AI-generated resume flags raise credibility concerns about the growth engineering and A/B testing claims.

If CGI is excluded, total qualifying experience is under 2 years — an immediate disqualifier. Recruiter must verify employment dates, graduation status, and whether CGI was full-time concurrent with or prior to the graduate degree before this profile can advance.
